name: npc-object-pool-cap
summary: Zone.exe pre-sizes the NPC object pool at 256 per process and gives kind 4 exactly 256 handles. A zone hosting many maps runs out and every further NPC is dropped with 'NPCManager::nm_SetNPC : Too many npc'. Raise the pool AND move kind 4's handle range above the rest of the handle space.
status: WORKING 2026-09-15 at npcs=1024: zone01 of the Fiesta2026on2016 smoke stack boots READY with 216 maps, ZERO 'Too many npc' asserts (35 on stock), no crash, and the NPCs past slot 256 get REAL handles (the puzzle-game AI scripts run clean). FOUR earlier attempts fell short - see history[]; the cap is SIX constants plus the handle range.

target.note: Chained builds need --allow-hash-mismatch; no other recipe touches these sites.

npcs.why: Two independent ceilings. A handle is a u16 so handle_base + npcs must stay under 0xFFFF (0xA000 leaves 24575). Memory is the practical one: each NPC object is 0x256C = 9580 bytes, so 1024 costs 9.8 MB and 2048 costs 19.6 MB on top of the stock 2.4 MB.

handle_base.why: It must sit ABOVE every other kind's range or the if-chain in sohu_HandleSplit will claim the handle for whichever kind tests first. The highest boundary in that function is 0x6232, so 0xA000 clears it with room.

why: NPCs are allocated from a typed object factory, so the assert is an ALLOCATION FAILURE, not a bounds check:
NPCManager::nm_SetNPC
0x004C6645   push 4                    ; object type 4 = NPC
0x004C664B   mov  ecx, 0x132826B8      ; the object manager singleton
0x004C6650   call 0x0054FE20           ; factory Alloc -> NULL when the pool is empty
0x004C6663   push 0x006C5AD0           ; "NPCManager::nm_SetNPC : Too many npc"
the factory switches on the type and each type has its own sub-pool; case 4 is [this+0xCC],
and the manager's ctor sizes them in turn:
0x0055765C   push 0x100  ; [esi+0xCC]   (256)   <-- the NPC pool
RAISING THE POOL ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH, and fails in a way that looks unrelated. A shine handle is a u16
carved into per-kind RANGES by sohu_HandleSplit (0x00633650), an if-chain of literal bounds:
<=0x1F40 kind 5 (mobs)   0x251C kind 2 (players)  0x2904 kind 3   0x34BC kind 1
0x42BC   kind 0          0x43BC kind 4 (NPCs)     0x4BBC kind 8   ... up to 0x6232
kind 4's span is EXACTLY 0x100 = the pool size. Give the pool 2048 slots and the 257th NPC gets handle
0x43BC, which that chain resolves to KIND 8 - som_GetObject then reads the wrong kind's slot table and the
zone melts (measured: 545 asserts, never READY).
Each block of the chain tests BOTH its bounds (`mov ecx,lower; cmp cx,ax; ja next; mov edx,upper;
cmp ax,dx; jae next`), so the blocks do not have to stay in ascending order: kind 4 can simply be moved
to a base above every other range, which leaves all the other kinds untouched. The two places that COMPOSE
an NPC handle (`add eax, 0x42BC`) move with it. The old 0x42BC..0x43BC gap is then unassigned, which is
correct - nothing issues handles there any more.
The pool's own storage needs no relocation: ShineObjectPool::Create (0x005546F0) heap-allocates
(count+1)*0xC for the slot table and som_GetObject bounds-checks the index against [pool+4], which this
patch raises with the count.
THE POOL IS ONLY HALF OF IT. A live read of a running zone (tools/zone_npcpool_probe.pl) showed the
NPC pool with 256 slots, ALL 256 carrying an object and the free list empty, the objects individually
allocated 0x256C apart. They come from a vector-new next to the mob one, which uses the same shape:
0x0055C6B6  push 0x256C04            ; 0x100 * 0x256C + 4 bytes
0x0055C6D8  push 0x100               ; eh vector ctor element count
0x0055C6E6  mov dword [eax], 0x100   ; array cookie, read by the dtor
0x0055C9E7  push 0x2568 / mov dword [eax], 0x1F40  <- the MOB array, 8000, same pattern
Raise the pool without the array and the extra slots hand back a NULL object, so nm_SetNPC asserts
on roughly the share of slots with no object: 512 slots gave 268 asserts, 2048 gave 545.
AND THE FILL LOOP HAS ITS OWN BOUND, which is what a live probe finally showed: with the pool at 1024
only 256 slots carried an object. The loop that attaches array elements to pool slots ends on a
SLOT-BYTE count, not on the pool count:
0x0055C7A4  add edi, 0x256C   ; next object
0x0055C7AD  cmp eax, 0xC00    ; 0xC00 = 256 * 12 -> exactly 256 attached
(the pool above it uses cmp eax, 0x4650 = 1500 * 12, the same shape)
A slot whose object is NULL is handed out by the factory and nm_SetNPC asserts on it, which is why
raising anything else alone made the assert count go UP rather than down.
AND EACH HANDLE MAKER RANGE-CHECKS THE INDEX against the kind's span before composing the handle:
0x00548F26  mov edx, 0x100 ; cmp dx, ax ; ja compose ; mov eax, 0xFFFF ; ret     (maker A)
0x00557C80  mov ecx, 0x100 ; cmp cx, ax ; ja compose ; mov esi, 0xFFFF ; ...     (maker B)
With the pool at 1024 but the checks at 256, NPC number 257 and up are CREATED (no assert) but carry handle
0xFFFF, the invalid handle. Nothing looks them up successfully: cIsObjectDead(0xFFFF) reports dead, and the
puzzle-game AI scripts (Xiaoming/Oluming/Toryming on Eld) took their dead branch, which indexes a nil global
and raised 'lss_Routine : function call error' 40 times a second. Seen by wrapping the routine in pcall and
logging the error through the cAssertLog binding: handle=65535 dead=1 ... attempt to index global 'PuzzleMemory'.
history: attempt 1 (pool only): the 257th NPC took handle 0x43BC, which sohu_HandleSplit resolves to KIND 8, so
som_GetObject read the wrong kind's slot table. Fixed by moving kind 4's range.
attempt 2 (pool + handles): still 545 asserts. The NPC OBJECTS come from a vector-new sized 0x100.
attempt 3 (pool + handles + object array): still 545. A live probe (tools/zone_npcpool_probe.pl in
Fiesta2026on2016) showed 1024 slots but only 256 with an object - the loop that ATTACHES objects to slots
ends on its own slot-byte bound, cmp eax, 0xC00 (= 256 * 12).
The lesson: a 'cap' in this exe can be several independent constants that must all move together, and the

attempt 4 (five constants + handles): READY and 0 asserts, but the puzzle NPCs' AI errored every tick. Their
  handle was 0xFFFF: both handle makers still checked index < 0x100 and returned the invalid handle above it.
way to find the rest is to read the live structure out of the running process, not more disassembly.

edits.why: ShineObjectManager ctor: NPC sub-pool (+0xCC) element count
NPC object array: operator new byte count (npcs * 0x256C + 4)
NPC object array: eh vector ctor element count
NPC object array: array cookie element count (the dtor reads it)
NPC pool fill loop: bound in SLOT BYTES (npcs * 12), the loop that attaches objects to slots
NPC handle maker A: index < span check (returns 0xFFFF, the invalid handle, above it)
NPC handle maker B: index < span check (returns 0xFFFF above it)

measured: 2026-09-15 Fiesta2026on2016 smoke stack, zone01 (Roumen/Elderine + SD_Vale00 + VoidDn), per boot:
stock                     : READY, 35 x 'Too many npc',  pool 256/256 slots with an object
pool only (2048)          : never READY, 545 asserts, EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION
pool only (512)           : never READY, 268 asserts, 2 crashes
pool+array+handles (1024) : never READY, 545 asserts - the FILL LOOP still stopped at 256
all four + handles (1024) : READY, 0 asserts, 0 crashes, pool 1024/1024 with an object   <-- this recipe
handles only (256)        : READY, 35 asserts - proves the handle move is harmless on its own
six constants + handles (1024): READY, 0 asserts, 0 lss_Routine errors (was ~40/s), puzzle NPCs have real handles
side_effects: NPCs that the stock zone silently DROPPED now spawn, which can expose content defects that were masked.
(The earlier note here blaming the puzzle-game scripts was wrong: their lss_Routine errors were THIS recipe's
missing maker-span edits, fixed in the same commit that added them.)
